review.plain: Stealing, maliciously damaging, receiving or concealing a stolen motor vehicle or trailer is punishable by up to 15 years in state prison; concealing a vehicle thief carries up to 10 years.
acts: steals a motor vehicle or trailer
maliciously damages a motor vehicle or trailer
buys, receives, possesses, conceals, or obtains control of a motor vehicle or trailer
takes a motor vehicle without the authority of the owner and steals from it any of its parts or accessories
conceals any motor vehicle or trailer thief

consequences: Prosecution may not be placed on file or continued without a finding for a second or subsequent offense

Court or magistrate reports a conviction or delinquency adjudication to the registrar of motor vehicles, who revokes the license or right to operate immediately; no appeal, motion for new trial or exceptions stays the revocation
Revocation lasts until 1 year after revocation for a first offense, or 5 years after revocation for a subsequent conviction or adjudication, unless the prosecution ends in the person's favor

Temporary release in an officer's custody may be granted by the commissioner of correction for a next-of-kin or spouse funeral, a critically ill close relative or spouse, or emergency medical services

crimes.act: Steals a motor vehicle or trailer

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $15,000, or both a fine and imprisonment
Not less than 1 year imprisonment; sentence not suspended or reduced until 1 year is served; not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release

crimes.act: Maliciously damages a motor vehicle or trailer

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $15,000, or both a fine and imprisonment
Not less than 1 year imprisonment; sentence not suspended or reduced until 1 year is served; not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release

consequences: Prosecution may not be placed on file or continued without a finding for a second or subsequent offense

Temporary release in an officer's custody may be granted by the commissioner of correction for a next-of-kin or spouse funeral, a critically ill close relative or spouse, or emergency medical services
Report to the registrar of motor vehicles and license revocation do not apply to a conviction or adjudication for malicious damage

crimes.act: Buys, receives, possesses, conceals, or obtains control of a motor vehicle or trailer
conditions: The motor vehicle or trailer was stolen
Intentional and malicious removal, defacing or alteration of an identifying number is prima facie evidence of knowledge
knowledge: Knowing or having reason to know the vehicle or trailer to have been stolen

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $15,000, or both a fine and imprisonment
Not less than 1 year imprisonment; sentence not suspended or reduced until 1 year is served; not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release

crimes.act: Takes a motor vehicle without the authority of the owner and steals from it any of its parts or accessories

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $15,000, or both a fine and imprisonment
Not less than 1 year imprisonment; sentence not suspended or reduced until 1 year is served; not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release

crimes.act: Conceals any motor vehicle or trailer thief

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years of imprisonment, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $5,000, or both

review.plain: Requires the owner to report a stolen vehicle, sets police notice duties when it is recovered, and requires restitution to the insurer after a conviction under the motor vehicle theft section.
Requires the owner of record of a burned motor vehicle to submit a signed statement to the fire department.

Larceny is stealing, or obtaining by false pretense or converting, another's property; it carries up to 5 years in state prison over $1,200 or for a firearm, and up to 10 years if the victim is 60 or older or disabled.
acts: steals
obtains by a false pretence
secretes
takes, carries away, conceals or copies
obtains by a false pretense

terms: "Property": includes money, personal chattels, notes, bonds, bills, books of accounts, deeds and writings, valuable contracts, receipts, releases, writs, process, certificates of title, public records, anything of the realty or annexed to it, a security deposit, electronically processed or stored data (tangible or intangible), data in transit, telecommunications services, and any domesticated animal including dogs, or a beast or bird ordinarily kept in confinement

crimes.act: Steals, obtains by a false pretence, or converts or secretes the property of another
conditions: The property belongs to another, whether or not in the person's possession at the time of conversion or secreting
intent: Unlawfully, and with intent to steal or embezzle (convert), or with intent to convert (secrete)

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $25,000 and up to 2 years in jail (firearm, or value exceeds $1,200)

penalties.if: the value of the property stolen, other than a firearm, does not exceed $1,200
penalties.penalty: Up to 1 year in jail or a fine of up to $1,500

crimes.act: Steals, obtains by a false pretense, or converts, secretes, unlawfully takes, carries away, conceals or copies any trade secret of another
conditions: The property is a trade secret of another, regardless of value
intent: Unlawfully, and with intent to steal or embezzle, or with intent to convert
terms: "Trade secret": anything tangible or intangible or electronically kept or stored, which constitutes, represents, evidences or records a secret scientific, technical, merchandising, production or management information, design, process, procedure, formula, invention or improvement

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $25,000 and up to 2 years in jail

crimes.act: Steals, obtains by a false pretense, or converts or secretes the property of a person 60 or older or with a disability
conditions: The owner is 60 years of age or older, or a person with a disability as defined in section 13K of chapter 265
intent: Unlawfully, and with intent to steal or embezzle, or with intent to convert
consequences: The court may order restitution to the victim commensurate with the value of the property, regardless of value

penalties.penalty: Where value exceeds $250: up to 10 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $50,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: the value of the property does not exceed $250
penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in the house of correction or a fine of up to $1,000, or both

review.plain: Shoplifting is intentionally taking, concealing or altering the price of store merchandise to deprive the merchant; under $250 it is a fine at first, and $250 or more carries up to 2½ years in the house of correction.
acts: takes possession of, carries away, transfers or causes to be carried away or transferred
conceals upon his person or otherwise
alters, transfers or removes any label, price tag or marking indicia of value
transfers any merchandise displayed, held, stored or offered for sale by any store or other retail mercantile establishment from the container
records a value for the merchandise which is less than the actual retail value
removes a shopping cart from the premises of a store or other retail mercantile establishment

consequences: Applies to the exclusion of the general larceny section when the retail value of the goods obtained is less than $250

penalties.penalty: Retail value under $250, first offense: a fine of up to $250
A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500

penalties.if: retail value under $250, third or subsequent offense
penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500, or up to 2 years in a jail, or both

penalties.if: retail value of the goods obtained equals or exceeds $250
penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or both

crimes.act: Takes possession of, carries away, transfers or causes to be carried away or transferred any merchandise offered for sale by a store or other retail mercantile establishment
ways: causes to be carried away or transferred
intent: With the intention of depriving the merchant of the possession, use of benefit of the merchandise or converting it to the person's use without paying the value

crimes.act: Conceals upon his person or otherwise any merchandise offered for sale by a store or other retail mercantile establishment
intent: With the intention of depriving the merchant of proceeds, use or benefit of the merchandise or converting it to the person's use without paying the value

crimes.act: Alters, transfers or removes any label, price tag or marking indicia of value affixed to merchandise and attempts to purchase it at less than full retail value
intent: With the intention of depriving the merchant of all or some part of the retail value

crimes.act: Transfers merchandise from the container in or on which it is displayed to any other container
intent: With intent to deprive the merchant of all or some part of the retail value

crimes.act: Records a value for the merchandise which is less than the actual retail value
intent: With the intention of depriving the merchant of the full retail value

crimes.act: Removes a shopping cart from the premises of a store or other retail mercantile establishment
conditions: Without the consent of the merchant given at the time of removal
intent: With the intention of permanently depriving the merchant of the possession, use or benefit of the cart

review.plain: Making, selling, possessing or using theft-detection shielding devices, or deactivators and removers, or deactivating or removing a theft detection device with intent to steal, carries up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: manufactures, sells, offers for sale or distributes a laminated or coated bag or other device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
possesses a laminated or coated bag or device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
possesses any tool or device designed or adapted to either:

manufacturers, sells, offers for sale or distributes a tool or device designed or adapted to allow the deactivation of a theft detection device or to allow the removal of a theft detection device from merchandise
deactivates or removes a theft detection device from merchandise prior to purchase, in a retail establishment

penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in a house of correction, or up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $25,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Manufactures, sells, offers for sale or distributes a laminated or coated bag or other device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
Possesses a laminated or coated bag or device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
intent: With the intent to commit, aid or abet a theft

crimes.act: Possesses any tool or device designed or adapted to allow the deactivation or removal of a theft detection device
ways: allow the deactivation of a theft detection device
allow the removal of a theft detection device from merchandise
intent: With the intent to use the tool or device to deactivate or remove a theft detection device on merchandise without the permission of the merchant or person owning or lawfully holding it

crimes.act: Manufactures, sells, offers for sale or distributes a tool or device designed or adapted to allow the deactivation of a theft detection device or to allow the removal of a theft detection device from merchandise
conditions: Without the permission of the merchant or person owning or lawfully holding the merchandise

crimes.act: Deactivates or removes a theft detection device from merchandise prior to purchase, in a retail establishment
intent: With the intent to steal the merchandise

review.plain: Possessing, using, making or counterfeiting retail receipts, price tickets or UPC labels to cheat a retailer is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: possesses, uses, utters, transfers, makes, alters, counterfeits or reproduces a retail sales or return receipt, price ticket or universal product code label

penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in a house of correction, or up to 5 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $10,000, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Possesses, uses, utters, transfers, makes, alters, counterfeits or reproduces a retail sales or return receipt, price ticket or universal product code label
intent: With intent to cheat or defraud a retailer

review.plain: Organized retail crime, theft of over $2,500 in retail goods with 2 or more others to resell, carries up to 10 years; over $10,000, up to 15 years; leading such an enterprise, up to 20 years.
acts: steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $2,500
steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $10,000
conspires with others as an organizer, supervisor, financier or manager, to commit an organized retail crime or an aggravated organized retail crime

terms: "Retail merchandise": 1 or more items of tangible personal property displayed, held, stored or offered for sale in a retail establishment

crimes.act: Steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $2,500
conditions: Acting in concert with 2 or more persons
Within a 180 day period
Merchandise valued at more than $2,500; a series of thefts from 1 or more mercantile establishments may be aggregated
intent: To resell or otherwise reenter the retail merchandise into commerce
consequences: May be prosecuted in any county where a theft from a mercantile establishment occurred

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in a state prison

crimes.act: Steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $10,000
conditions: Acting in concert with 2 or more persons
Within a 180 day period
Merchandise valued at more than $10,000; a series of thefts from 1 or more mercantile establishments may be aggregated
intent: To resell or otherwise reenter the retail merchandise into commerce
consequences: May be prosecuted in any county where a theft from a mercantile establishment occurred

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in a state prison

crimes.act: Conspires with others as an organizer, supervisor, financier or manager, to commit an organized retail crime or an aggravated organized retail crime
conditions: The person acts as an organizer, supervisor, financier or manager

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $250,000 or 5 times the retail value of the merchandise seized at the time of the arrest, whichever is greater, or up to 20 years in state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment

review.plain: Obtaining a person's signature on a written instrument by false pretense and with intent to defraud is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: obtains the signature of a person to a written instrument

crimes.act: Obtains by a false pretence the signature of a person to a written instrument
conditions: The false making of the written instrument would be a forgery

penalties.penalty: Up to 10 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $500 and up to 2 years in jail

review.plain: A ship captain who embezzles or fraudulently converts money, goods or property belonging to the crew, owners or suppliers of the vessel is guilty of larceny.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property, held or possessed by or delivered to him

crimes.act: Embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property, held or possessed by or delivered to him
conditions: The property belongs wholly or in part to the crew, the owners of the vessel, or those who furnished supplies to the vessel
Applies although he is a joint charterer or co-partner with the crew, owners or suppliers

penalties.penalty: Guilty of larceny; the punishment is set in another section of the law

review.plain: Obtaining a note, release, extension of time, or contract change by false pretense, or bank credit by a false written financial statement, with intent to defraud, is larceny.
acts: obtains by a false pretence the making, acceptance or endorsement of a bill of exchange or promissory note, the release or substitution of collateral or other security, an extension of time for the payment of an obligation, or the release or alteration of the obligation of a written contract
obtains for himself or for any other person credit from any bank or trust company

penalties.penalty: Guilty of larceny; the punishment is set in another section of the law

crimes.act: Obtains by a false pretence the making, acceptance or endorsement of a bill of exchange or promissory note, the release or substitution of collateral or other security, an extension of time for the payment of an obligation, or the release or alteration of the obligation of a written contract

Obtains for himself or for any other person credit from any bank or trust company or any banking institution or any mortgage lender, or any retail seller of goods or services accustomed to give credit, by a false statement in writing respecting the financial condition, or means or ability to pay, of himself or of any other person

review.plain: Fraudulently obtaining, attempting to obtain, or helping another obtain a commercial computer service is punishable by up to 2½ years in a house of correction.
acts: obtains, or attempts to obtain, or aids or abets another in obtaining, any commercial computer service by false representation, false statement, unauthorized charging to the account of another, by installing or tampering with any facilities or equipment or by any other means

terms: "Commercial computer service": the use of computers, computer systems, computer programs or computer networks, or the access to or copying of the data, where such use, access or copying is offered by the proprietor or operator to others on a subscription or other basis for monetary consideration

crimes.act: Obtains, or attempts to obtain, or aids or abets another in obtaining, any commercial computer service
ways: aids or abets another in obtaining
conditions: By false representation, false statement, unauthorized charging to the account of another, by installing or tampering with any facilities or equipment or by any other means

penalties.penalty: Up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $3,000, or both

review.plain: Inducing another by false pretense and with intent to defraud to part with property, or with benefits described in the contract and computer-service fraud provisions, is larceny.
acts: induces another to part with property of any kind or with any of the benefits described in sections 33 and 33A

crimes.act: Induces another to part with property of any kind or with any of the benefits described in sections 33 and 33A
conditions: By a false pretence

penalties.penalty: Guilty of larceny; the punishment is set in another section of the law

review.plain: Says the general larceny, signature and inducement sections do not apply to a purchase by false pretense about means to pay when payment is not due at delivery, unless the pretense is in a signed writing.

Making or using false material statements in the mortgage lending process, or receiving proceeds of such fraud, carries up to 5 years in state prison; a pattern across 3 or more properties carries up to 15 years.
acts: makes or causes to be made any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission
uses, or facilitates the use of, any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission
receives any proceeds or any other funds in connection with a residential mortgage closing
files or causes to be filed with a registrar of deeds any document that contains a material statement that is false or a material omission
engages in a pattern of residential mortgage fraud

terms: "Material omission": the omission or concealment of a material fact necessary to prevent a statement from being misleading, in the light of the circumstances under which the statement is made

"Mortgage lending process": the process through which a person seeks or obtains a residential mortgage loan, including solicitation, application, origination, negotiation of terms, third-party provider services, underwriting, signing and closing, and funding of the loan

"Residential mortgage loan": a loan or agreement to extend credit made to a person, secured by a mortgage, security interest, deed to secure debt, deed of trust, or other document representing a security interest or lien upon any interest in a 1 to 4 family residential property located in the commonwealth, including renewal or refinancing
consequences: If the violation results from conduct or omission of an employee or agent, the court may consider as mitigating factors that the defendant maintained and enforced a written policy prohibiting such conduct and provided it to the employee or agent before the violation

crimes.act: Makes or causes to be made any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission, during or in connection with the mortgage lending process
intent: With the intent that the statement be relied upon by a mortgage lender, borrower or any other party to the mortgage lending process
knowledge: Knowing the statement to be false or to contain a material omission

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $10,000 for a natural person or up to $100,000 for any other person, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Uses, or facilitates the use of, any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission, during or in connection with the mortgage lending process
intent: With the intent that the statement be relied upon by a mortgage lender, borrower or any other party to the mortgage lending process
knowledge: Knowing the statement to be false or to contain a material omission

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $10,000 for a natural person or up to $100,000 for any other person, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Receives any proceeds or any other funds in connection with a residential mortgage closing
knowledge: Knowing such proceeds or funds were obtained in violation of clause (1) or (2)

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $10,000 for a natural person or up to $100,000 for any other person, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Files or causes to be filed with a registrar of deeds any document that contains a material statement that is false or a material omission
knowledge: Knowing the document to contain a material statement that is false or a material omission

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, or up to 2½ years in the house of correction, or a fine of up to $10,000 for a natural person or up to $100,000 for any other person, or both a fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Engages in a pattern of residential mortgage fraud
conditions: Violation of subsection (b) in connection with 3 or more residential properties
terms: "Pattern of residential mortgage fraud": violation of subsection (b) in connection with 3 or more residential properties

penalties.penalty: Up to 15 years in state prison, or a fine of up to $50,000 for a natural person or up to $500,000 for any other person, or both a fine and imprisonment

review.plain: Making or passing a check with intent to defraud, knowing there are insufficient funds, is attempted larceny, and larceny if money, property or services are obtained.
acts: makes, draws, utters or delivers any check, draft or order for the payment of money upon any bank or other depositary

terms: "Credit": an arrangement or understanding with the bank or depositary for the payment of such check, draft or order

crimes.act: Makes, draws, utters or delivers any check, draft or order for the payment of money upon any bank or other depositary
conditions: Refusal of payment by the drawee is prima facie evidence of intent to defraud and knowledge of insufficient funds
defenses: The maker or drawer paid the holder the amount due, with all costs and protest fees, within two days after receiving notice of non-payment
knowledge: With knowledge that the maker or drawer has not sufficient funds or credit at such bank or other depositary for payment

penalties.penalty: Guilty of attempted larceny; the punishment is set in another section of the law

penalties.if: money or property or services are obtained
penalties.penalty: Guilty of larceny; the punishment is set in another section of the law

review.plain: Defines terms such as credit card, cardholder, issuer, receives and falsely makes for the credit card misuse sections.
Misusing a credit card with intent to defraud, such as stealing, selling, forging a signature or using one for up to $1,200, is punishable by up to 1 year in jail or a $2,500 fine.
acts: makes or causes to be made, either directly or indirectly, any false statement as to a material fact in writing
takes a credit card from the person, possession, custody or control of another without the cardholder's consent by any conduct which would constitute larceny
receives the credit card
receives a credit card that he knows to have been lost, mislaid, or delivered under a mistake as to the identity or address of the cardholder
sells a credit card, or buys a credit card from a person other than the issuer or his authorized agent
signs a credit card

uses, for the purpose of obtaining money, goods, services or anything else of value, a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked

obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued

furnishes money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card which he knows was obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
fails to furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value which he represents in writing to the issuer that he has furnished
receives money, goods, services or anything else of value obtained in violation of clauses (f) to (i), inclusive
makes a false statement in reporting a credit card to be lost or stolen

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $2,500, or up to 1 year in a jail or house of correction, or both

consequences: A person discovered by a police officer in the act of violating this section may be arrested without a warrant

crimes.act: Makes or causes to be made any false statement as to a material fact in writing respecting his identity or that of any other person, or his financial condition or that of any other person, for the purpose of procuring the issuance of a credit card
intent: With intent that it be relied on

crimes.act: Takes a credit card from the person, possession, custody or control of another without the cardholder's consent by any conduct which would constitute larceny
conditions: Possessing or controlling stolen credit cards issued in the names of four or more other persons gives rise to a presumption of violation

crimes.act: Receives the credit card, with knowledge that it has been so taken
knowledge: With knowledge that it has been so taken
intent: With intent to use it or to sell it, or to transfer it to a person other than the issuer or cardholder

crimes.act: Receives a credit card that he knows to have been lost, mislaid, or delivered under a mistake as to the identity or address of the cardholder, and retains possession
knowledge: Knowing the card to have been lost, mislaid, or delivered under a mistake as to the identity or address of the cardholder
intent: With intent to use it or to sell it or to transfer it to a person other than the issuer or the cardholder

crimes.act: Sells a credit card, or buys a credit card from a person other than the issuer or his authorized agent
crimes.who: A person other than the issuer or his authorized agent

crimes.act: Signs a credit card
crimes.who: A person other than the cardholder or a person authorized by him

crimes.act: Uses, for the purpose of obtaining money, goods, services or anything else of value, a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
conditions: The value of money, goods or services obtained is not in excess of $1,200

crimes.act: Obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued
conditions: The value of money, goods or services obtained is not in excess of $1,200

crimes.act: Furnishes money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card which he knows was obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
conditions: The value of the goods or services obtained is not in excess of $1,200
crimes.who: A person authorized by an issuer to furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card by the cardholder, or any agent or employee of such person
knowledge: Knowing the card was obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), or is forged, expired or revoked

crimes.act: Fails to furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value which he represents in writing to the issuer that he has furnished
conditions: The difference between the value actually furnished and the value represented to the issuer does not exceed $1,200
crimes.who: A person authorized by an issuer to furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card by the cardholder, or any agent or employee of such person

crimes.act: Receives money, goods, services or anything else of value obtained in violation of clauses (f) to (i), inclusive
Makes a false statement in reporting a credit card to be lost or stolen

review.plain: Fraudulent credit card use over $1,200, false making or embossing of cards, and possessing incomplete cards or card-making equipment is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison or a $10,000 fine.
acts: obtains control over a credit card as security for debt
receives a credit card which he knows was taken or retained under circumstances which constitute credit card theft
falsely makes or falsely embosses a purported credit card or utters such a credit card

obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by use of a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, of section thirty-seven B, or by use of a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked

obtains money, goods or services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued

furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card which he knows was obtained in violation of subsections (b) to (e), inclusive, of section thirty-seven B, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
fails to furnish money, goods or services or anything else of value which he represents in writing to the issuer that he has furnished
receives money, goods, services or anything else of value obtained in violation of subsections (f) or (g) of section thirty-seven B
possesses one or more incomplete credit cards
machinery, plates or any other contrivance designed to reproduce instruments purporting to be the credit cards of an issuer who has not consented to the preparation of such credit cards

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $10,000, or up to 2½ years in a jail or house of correction, or up to 5 years in state prison, or both a fine and imprisonment

consequences: A person discovered by a police officer in the act of violating this section may be arrested without a warrant

crimes.act: Obtains control over a credit card as security for debt

Receives a credit card which he knows was taken or retained under circumstances which constitute credit card theft or a violation of clause (a) or (d) of the credit card misuse section or clause (a) of this section
knowledge: Knowing the card was so taken or retained

crimes.act: Falsely makes or falsely embosses a purported credit card or utters such a credit card
conditions: Possessing or controlling four or more falsely embossed credit cards gives rise to a presumption of violation
terms: "Falsely embosses": completion of a credit card, without the authorization of the named issuer, by adding any of the matter, other than the signature of the cardholder, which an issuer requires to appear on the credit card before it can be used

"Falsely makes": making or drawing, in whole or in part, a device or instrument which purports to be the credit card of a named issuer but which the issuer did not authorize, or altering a validly issued credit card

crimes.act: Obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by use of a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e) of the credit card misuse section, or by use of a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
conditions: The value of the money, goods or services obtained is in excess of $1,200

crimes.act: Obtains money, goods or services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued

"Personal identifying information": any name or number that may be used, alone or in conjunction with any other information, to assume the identity of an individual, including any name, address, telephone number, driver's license number, social security number, place of employment, employee identification number, mother's maiden name, demand deposit account number, savings account number, credit card number or computer password identification
